result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps, providing a baseline level of safety. However, the wide roadway and lack of a median refuge island result in significant exposure time for pedestrians crossing multiple lanes of traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a midpoint refuge, increasing exposure to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground and center.

hazards.name: Lack of Median Refuge
hazards.description: The absence of a median or refuge island means pedestrians have no safe place to wait if they cannot complete the crossing in one signal cycle.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and continuous sidewalks within a residential context. However, the wide roadway width and lack of a median refuge island increase pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic during crossings.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a median refuge, increasing exposure time to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground zebra crosswalk across the main roadway.

hazards.name: High-speed roadway design
hazards.description: Wide lanes and signalized control on a through-street can encourage vehicle speeds that are unsafe for a residential pedestrian environment.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway approaches to the intersection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island at the crosswalk to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalks, ADA-compliant curb ramps with tactile warning pads, and pedestrian signals. Safety is further enhanced by a 'No Turn On Red' restriction, although the intersection lacks physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction from vegetation
hazards.description: Dense trees and bushes on the corner may partially obscure pedestrians waiting to cross from the view of approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Constructing curb extensions would reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers by placing pedestrians further into the roadway before crossing.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Implementing an LPI would allow pedestrians to enter the crosswalk several seconds before vehicles are permitted to turn, increasing their visibility and priority.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and overhead traffic signals within a residential setting. However, the environment lacks visible pedestrian-specific signal heads and traffic calming measures, which may increase risk for those crossing the street.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

hazards.name: Wide Corner Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry on the right appears wide, which can encourage higher vehicle speeds during right turns.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.
